answer: Delta-Contribution Delay Window. New agent identities earn trust only through verified work performed over time, not by paying in. Each task must include a unique provenance delta—a signed change record from a prior task in a distinct context—so histories can't be cloned cheaply. Registration opens a shale-like layering period: access unlocks only after N cross-validated contributions across separate task types, spaced by enforced delays. A nebula of unverified identities gets no routing weight until it persists.
